item.title: Global Smartphone Market to Grow in 2025 as Memory Shortage Drives Price Pressures for 2026
item.description: Worldwide smartphone shipments are expected to rise in 2025, with IDC forecasting a 1.5% year-over-year increase to about 1.25 billion units. The improved outlook reflects stronger demand for Apple devices, firmer results in key emerging markets, and steadier conditions in China. IDC raised its forecast following Apple’s faster-than-expected momentum entering the holiday quarter. Apple’s performance accounts for a substantial part of the improved forecast. item.title: Early Smartphone Use Associated With Sleep Problems and Mental Health Issues in Preteens
item.description: Twelve-year-olds who owned smartphones had higher odds of depression, obesity, and sleep problems compared to peers without smartphones, according to a study published December 1, 2025, in the journal Pediatrics. Researchers analyzed data from 10,588 children and adolescents across 21 sites between 2016 and 2022. item.title: Are Meeting Overloads Quietly Damaging Employee Well-Being?
item.description: Anyone working in an organisation knows it: meetings follow one after another at a frantic pace. On average, managers spend 23 hours a week in meetings. Much of what happens in them is considered to be of low value, or even entirely counterproductive. The paradox is that bad meetings generate even more meetings… in an attempt to repair the damage caused by previous ones. Image: Rodeo Project Management Software / UnsplashAnd yet, for a long time, meetings were not subject of management research.

item.title: Meta Removes 134 Million Scam Ads and Disrupts 12 Million Accounts to Combat Online Scams
item.description: Meta Platforms has removed more than 134 million scam advertisements across its family of apps in 2025. The company also disrupted nearly 12 million accounts linked to organized criminal operations in the first half of the year. Meta’s actions extend across Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp. The social media giant says it has expanded artificial intelligence and facial recognition technology to detect and remove content exploiting celebrity images for scams.
